chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad Hafs ibn Salim al-Hannat said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who freed a young slave girl who had not yet reached maturity, and her mother, before dying, had asked him to free a neck (herself) from her own wealth, so he bought her and freed her after her mother died. To whom would the walayah (manumying right) of the freed person belong? He said: 'Her walayah belongs to her mother's relatives from the father's side, and their maintenance is upon them until she reaches maturity and becomes self-sufficient.' He said: 'And the one who freed her on behalf of her mother has no share of her walayah.'

key_terms.رَقَبَةً: Raqabah (a slave's neck, referring to manumission)
key_terms.مِنْ قِبَلِ أَبِيهَا: Min qibali abiha (from the father's side)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the walayah of a slave girl freed after her mother's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific case of *umm al-walad* (mother of a child) manumission, ruling that when a master frees a young slave girl to fulfill her mother's bequest, the right of *walayah* (kinship/manumission bond) reverts to the mother's paternal relatives rather than the master. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining inheritance and maintenance (*nafaqah*) obligations, ensuring the freed woman remains under the care of her maternal lineage until she becomes self-sufficient.
